title: The pillars, reviewed
hook: five pillars, now understood from the inside

segments.voice: Yesterday: your balance, Salman's line, and each thing its right. Your line was give each its right.

Five words fit on an index card: testimony, prayer, zakat, fasting, pilgrimage. A visitor to a mosque could learn the list over one cup of tea. You met them on day nine, as a house built on five. This year stayed a long while inside each one: the words of the testimony, the standing and bowing of the prayer, the arithmetic and the mercy of zakat, the long afternoons of the fast, the white cloth of the pilgrimage. Now the year is closing, and these last days gather what it taught. First, the pillars, from the inside.
screen: `FIVE WORDS ON AN INDEX CARD.` → `A LONG WHILE INSIDE EACH ONE.` → `NOW, FROM THE INSIDE.`

segments.voice: In Sahih al-Bukhari, in paraphrase, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, says Islam is built on five: bearing witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His messenger, establishing the prayer, giving zakat, the pilgrimage, and fasting Ramadan. Built on: a house, not a checklist. Now each one from the inside. The testimony is said with the tongue, and Muslim teachers say it has to be meant: words that count when they're sincere. The prayer: the Qur'an praises the believers "Who are humble in their prayers." Standing and bowing are the outside; that humility, khushu', is the inside. Zakat: the Qur'an tells the Prophet to take alms from people's wealth to purify them, in paraphrase. The giving cleans the giver, not only feeds the poor. The fast: in Pickthall's Qur'an, fasting is prescribed "that ye may ward off (evil)." The hunger is the outside; the guarding is the inside. The pilgrimage: the Qur'an says the flesh and blood of the sacrifice don't reach Allah, but the devotion of the people does, in paraphrase. Each pillar has a body and a heart. In Muslim teaching, the body is required: the movements, the amounts, the days. And the texts keep pointing past the body to what it carries. Not skipping the outside, but finding what it holds. And the pillars lean on each other. The prayer holds the day. The fast holds a month. The pilgrimage, for whoever is able, can hold a whole life.
screen: `BUILT ON FIVE: A HOUSE, NOT A LIST.` · `EACH PILLAR HAS A BODY AND A HEART.` · `HUMBLE IN PRAYER, GUARDED IN THE FAST.` · `THE PILLARS LEAN ON EACH OTHER.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind the next prayer of the day, the one coming after this lesson. If you pray, decide now where you'll be when it comes, and plan to stop for it when it arrives, not after. If you don't, choose that same moment anyway, and when it comes, pause for one breath and remember that somewhere, someone is standing for that prayer just then.
The pillars. The five things Islam is built on, in the hadith's words: testimony, prayer, zakat, pilgrimage and fasting, each with a body and a heart. Today's word.
Your line: from the inside. The body of each pillar carries a heart. That's day one thousand four hundred twelve.

howItsDone: Muslims keep the pillars as acts with set forms: saying the testimony, praying the daily prayers at their times, paying zakat on qualifying wealth, fasting the month of Ramadan, and making the Hajj if able; teachers stress the intention and humility behind each act.

options: The movements are required, and they carry an inside too, like humility in prayer.
Yes. Each pillar is a ritual; what's inside you doesn't come into it.
No. Only the pilgrimage has an inside; the other pillars are just rules.
